narrative.thesis: The overall view is Hold: the rule-based model says Sell with fair value USD 110.03, while brokers are uniformly positive (median target USD 322.50, +72.8%). The financials show an outstanding business — FY2026 revenue grew 65.5% to USD 215,938mn, operating margin was 60.4% and net cash USD 54.1bn — but the model's Sell is a valuation call, not a verdict on quality. The judge sided with the bear on medium conviction: cash conversion of 0.86x and accruals of +10.9% are a conceded earnings-quality flag, and the bull's DCF upside was excluded as an outlier. The swing factor is whether that cash gap is working-capital timing or genuine deterioration.
key_takeaways: FY2026 revenue grew 65.5% to USD 215,938mn, a 68.3% four-year CAGR, though growth slowed from +114.2% to +65.5%.
ROE of 101.5% is driven by a 55.6% net margin and 1.36x asset turnover; the 1.35x multiplier adds little.
Cash conversion of 0.86x and accruals of +10.9% are the key earnings-quality flag.
The rule-based model says Sell at USD 110.03, below all 30 broker targets; brokers' median is USD 322.50.
The 38.1x P/E sits at the 6th percentile of five years versus a 64.1x median, though 23.6x TTM conflicts.
The overall view is Hold, a compromise between a cautious model and uniformly positive brokers.
narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA is a data center scale AI infrastructure company, operating through Compute & Networking and Graphics segments. Its GPU architectures and networking platforms serve accelerated computing and AI workloads, with a one-year product cadence now moving toward the Rubin platform; Blackwell architectures represented the majority of Data Center revenue in FY2026.

Data center products were 89.7% of FY2026 revenue (USD 193.7bn), with gaming 7.4%, professional visualization 1.5%, automotive 1.1% and OEM/other 0.3%. The United States was 69.3% of revenue, Taiwan 19.6% and Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1%. The 10-K flags competition as a risk, but NVIDIA's operating margin of 66.2% (TTM) exceeds the 54.3% peer median, reflecting a leading position in AI accelerators.
narrative.financial_analysis:
Revenue rose from USD 26,914mn in FY2022 to USD 215,938mn in FY2026, a 68.3% four-year CAGR, though growth slowed to +65.5% in FY2026 from +114.2% and +125.9%. Gross margin expanded from 64.9% to 71.1% and operating margin from 37.3% to 60.4%, with SG&A falling to 2.1% of revenue and R&D to 8.6% from 19.6% in FY2022. Net margin reached 55.6% and ROE 101.5%.

The balance sheet is a fortress: cash and short-term investments of USD 62,556mn against USD 8,468mn of debt, net debt/EBITDA of -0.41x and interest cover of 503.4x. The blemish is earnings quality: cash conversion slipped to 0.86x, accruals rose to +10.9% and receivable days reached 52, so profit is running ahead of cash.
narrative.valuation_overview:
The DCF base case is USD 260.26 (+39.4%) on a 12.0% WACC, 2.5% terminal growth and 44.8% FCF margin, with a sensitivity range of USD 223.98–310.18 and 82% of 5,000 Monte Carlo draws above the price. The reverse DCF shows the price implies 41.9% annual revenue growth versus a 50.9% base case. Against its own five-year history the 38.1x P/E sits at the 6th percentile versus a 64.1x median, though the quoted 23.6x TTM conflicts with this.

The rule-based rating, however, excludes the DCF as an outlier (+122% vs the median of methods) and blends peer P/E of 103.02 and peer EV/EBITDA of 117.03 to a fair value of USD 110.03 (-41.0%), below all 30 broker targets. That gap between the DCF and the peer-multiple blend is the central valuation uncertainty.

rebuttals.response: The rule-based Sell rests on peer P/E 103.02 and EV/EBITDA 117.03, yet the DCF base case is USD 260.26 and 82% of Monte Carlo draws clear the price; the model sits below all 30 broker targets.
One-year weakness is real, but the 3Y and 5Y records are +313.3% and +518.3% versus +69.0% and +56.9%, and the 50/200-day cross is Positive.
Deceleration from +114.2% to +65.5% is off a far larger base; the 4Y CAGR is 68.3% and consensus FY2027E revenue growth is +90.6%, with FY2028E at +68.2%.

The 68.3% CAGR is backward-looking; FY2026 growth already halved to +65.5%. Consensus +90.6% requires reacceleration, and the model's own reverse DCF only needs +41.9% — the bar is set by guidance, not history.
Margins are strong but cash backs them poorly: cash conversion 0.86x and accruals +10.9% mean profit is outrunning cash. Pricing power that doesn't convert to cash is a quality risk, not a moat.

The DCF is an outlier: USD 260.26 is +122% vs the median of methods and was excluded from the rating. The rule-based blend lands at USD 110.03, below all 30 broker targets — the DCF is the least reliable input.

The 38.1x P/E is below its five-year median of 64.1x, so the multiple is not at a historical extreme.
deep.verdict: The bear case is stronger because its two load-bearing points survive rebuttal: cash conversion of 0.86x with accruals +10.9% is a conceded earnings-quality flag [S9, E18, E77], and the bull’s DCF upside is an excluded outlier [E88]. Bull operating strength is real [S1, S6, S10], but it does not resolve those risks.

deep.change_my_mind: A quarter of cash conversion above 1.0x with accruals reversing, plus FY2027 guidance at or above +90.6% revenue growth, would flip me to bull.

Growth: Bull reads S1/S2/E85/E86 as durable compounding; Bear reads E9/E65/E85 as deceleration needing unproven reacceleration.

deep.variant_view: The overall view is Hold, a compromise between the rule-based Sell (fair value USD 110.03) and uniformly positive brokers (median target USD 322.50, 16 Buy and 14 Outperform). The model is more cautious than every one of the 30 broker targets, largely because it excludes the DCF as an outlier and leans on peer multiples. This analysis sides with the judge's medium-conviction bear case on earnings quality, but sees the valuation gap as unresolved rather than settled in either direction.
deep.pre_mortem: If the case fails over the next 12 months, the most likely reasons are that cash conversion of 0.86x and accruals of +10.9% prove genuine earnings-quality deterioration, and that FY2027 growth undershoots the +90.6% consensus after FY2026's slowdown to +65.5%. A further leg down in the already-negative technical picture, or tighter export controls, would compound the de-rating.

company.description: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
